newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Some new faces in top slots on NZ First party list.
newsitem.headline: Some new faces in top slots on NZ First party list.

text.p: The opposition New Zealand First Party has issued its party list of candidates for the October 12 election with a smattering of new faces among the top contenders.
The list was chosen by a ballot of 80 party officials.

Leader Winston Peters tops the list, followed by his deputy Tau Henare. Third place goes to former Labour candidate the Reverend Ann Batten while former National MP and the party's employment spokesman Peter McCardle is at number four.
The party's other MP, former Labour MP Jack Elder is ranked seventh.

Party president Doug Woolerton is ranked eighth, while NZ First researcher Deborah Morris, 26, is a surprise inclusion at number nine. Former television journalist Tukuroirangi Morgan is ranked tenth.
On current polling the party could expect to win between 20 and 25 seats, leaving dumped spokesmen Rex Widerstrom and Terry Heffernan at 28 and 30 needing to win their constituency seats.
Heffernan has high hopes in Albany which contains a large slice of the old East Coast Bays seat with a history of strong third party support.
But Widerstrom has only a slim chance in Ohariu-Belmont where Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne has a commanding lead in two recent polls.
